reasoning_input.question_text: Prove by mathematical induction that, for all positive integers n: Σ(r=1 to n) r(r+1) = n(n+1)(n+2)/3

student_steps.content: When n=1: 1·2 = 2 and 1·2·3/3 = 2. True for n=1.
Therefore the formula is true for all positive integers n.

steps.description: Verify base case n=1: LHS = 2, RHS = 1·2·3/3 = 2
State the inductive hypothesis for n=k clearly and correctly
State what needs to be proven for n=k+1
Split the sum: Σ(k+1) = Σ(k) + (k+1)(k+2) and apply the hypothesis
Correctly factorise and simplify the algebra to reach (k+1)(k+2)(k+3)/3
State the conclusion clearly, invoking the principle of induction
steps.expected_expression: True for all n ∈ ℤ⁺ by the principle of mathematical induction
